title: release·CAS·canary·rollback

schema_change.rationale: release lane is a pure CAS structure; durable persistence reuses the WP02 ledger when wired

verification.ruff: 0 findings in WP21-owned paths under cyrano/configs/quality/ruff.toml
verification.formatter: ruff format --check clean on WP21-owned paths
verification.dev_check: dev.py check exit 0 after docs regeneration
verification.quality_gate: 0 findings in WP21-owned paths; pre-existing baseline debt unchanged

architecture.releases: prepare_release refuses without a human approval_id or scoped delegation (RELEASE_APPROVAL_REQUIRED); ReleaseLane.promote is CAS: evaluated-digest drift -> APPROVAL_INVALID, stale parent -> STALE_REVISION, pointer moves only on success; revoke marks durably; rollback moves the live pointer while history persists
architecture.rollout: assign_canary pins an explicit cohort to the live release; bind_dispatch checks revocation first (revoked run or revoked pin -> paused), binds post-promotion runs to live, keeps pre-promotion runs on known pins, pauses unknown pins; stop_dispatch reports the stopped state
architecture.recovery: rollback_or_revoke moves the pointer (default parent for live revoke, explicit target otherwise, no move when revoking a non-live release), reports impacted sessions separately, stops new dispatch only when the live pointer is affected, and never reverts user code

review_findings_resolved: approval dict without approval_id fabricated a delegation:False ref -> refused
revoking a non-live release rolled the live pointer back -> pointer only moves for live revoke or explicit target
bind_dispatch bound new runs to a revoked live release -> paused
